title: Novel Method for Removal of Orally Deposited Inhaled Fluticasone Propionate
official: A Proof-of-Concept Study of a Novel Method for Removal of Residual Oropharyngeal Inhaled Corticosteroid Deposits in Asthma
summary:
This study aims to determine whether an extra virgin olive oil-based water (EVOOW) mixture removes more fluticasone propionate (FP) from the mouth than water alone. More effective removal of residual FP deposits may help reduce the risk of complications associated with inhaled corticosteroid use, including obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), oral candidiasis (thrush), and speech and swallowing dysfunction.

Participants will attend two separate testing visits, during which they will rinse and gargle with either EVOOW or water, after receiving 1 puff if fluticasone propionate. The visits will be scheduled 7-10 days apart. Total participation will last up to 3 weeks.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy adults and adults with asthma, age 18 years and older
* Willing to hold orally and nasally inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) for 24h and 12h, respectively, before study visits with mouthwash sample collections (Visit 2 and Visit 3)
* No systemic or topical ocular corticosteroid use for the prior 4 weeks.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known hypersensitivity to fluticasone propionate
* Allergy to olives or olive oil
* Known allergy to oxymetazoline
* Current smoking or vaping
* Currently pregnant or trying to become pregnant.
